statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Delayed NQ has rotated from the session high back near the low, but the full intraday path remains two-sided rather than persistently one-way.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail remains below the blocking threshold; the U.S. cash open through the Dallas Fed release is the concentrated next structure checkpoint.
headline: NQ returns near the session low, but two-sided rotation keeps Tail at WATCH
body: Delayed NQ was 29,428.25 at 07:49 ET, down 0.22% from the 29,491.75 prior close after a 29,409.75–29,533.75 session range. The reversal from the high to near the low raises near-term path sensitivity, but meaningful two-sided movement remains evident. Brent above $90, higher volatility and elevated Treasury yields keep Stress extreme.

lookbackSummary: Tail was 19% through 20:00 UTC on August 30, rose with renewed U.S.-Iran escalation, peaked at 30% at 01:00 UTC, then eased as overnight and European trading rotated. It briefly returned to 26% at 08:00 before settling back into WATCH through 11:00 UTC.
outlookSummary: Tail is 23% WATCH because NQ has rotated back near the session low after earlier reaching the high, showing directional pressure but also substantial mean reversion. The 13:30–15:30 UTC U.S. cash-open/Dallas Fed window is the next concentrated test; persistent extension with weak pullbacks would be needed for a block.

forecast.analysis: Delayed NQ is 29,428.25 at 07:49 ET, down 0.22% and only 18.5 points above the 29,409.75 session low after earlier reaching 29,533.75. The full high-to-low rotation shows two-sided price discovery rather than a persistent no-retracement trend, keeping Tail in WATCH despite extreme background Stress.

forecast.analysis: Power-hour conditions raise conditional Tail because late-session positioning can accelerate an established move. The score stays below the block threshold unless the cash session is already holding near an extreme with failed retracements.

After the U.S. cash close, Tail falls toward the lower WATCH boundary if the session ends with rotation rather than one-way extension. Any unresolved late geopolitical headline remains a source of Stress rather than proof of directional persistence.
drivers: Whether the session closes near an extreme

forecast.analysis: During early post-close trade, a completed two-sided U.S. session would support a low Tail reading. Thin liquidity can amplify headlines, but without persistent price-path evidence the baseline remains normal.
drivers: Absence or presence of fresh catalysts

forecast.analysis: Later U.S. evening trade is expected to stay low-Tail if no new catalyst appears and NQ remains away from a sustained session extreme. Background energy and rate pressure keeps Stress high even under normal price structure.

As Asian liquidity begins to build, Tail moves back to WATCH if overnight price discovery starts testing a range edge. The key condition is whether any initial move receives meaningful counter-trend rotation.
Early Asia remains a conditional range test. Tail stays near 20% unless a geopolitical or rates impulse aligns with a directional NQ break and retracements become shallow.

Around the main Asian opening window, Tail edges higher because fresh regional flows can reinforce an overnight move. Sustained extension after failed pullbacks would be required for a materially higher band.

Asian cash-session development keeps Tail in WATCH while the market tests whether overnight direction broadens across regional equities and technology. Conflicting cross-asset signals would favor rotation rather than persistence.

If Asia settles into balanced trade, Tail eases toward the lower WATCH boundary. A renewed oil or yield shock would raise Stress first; Tail would rise only if NQ also develops efficient one-way structure.
Late Asian trade should remain near lower WATCH if meaningful retracements continue. A session-extreme hold across multiple hours would be the clearest condition for a higher Tail estimate.

Into the Europe pre-open, Tail remains contained unless overnight direction survives several pullback attempts. Cross-asset confirmation from yields, oil and technology futures would matter more than headline risk alone.

European pre-market positioning keeps Tail around 20% if NQ remains rotational. A large gap or an aligned rates-and-equities move would increase the probability of a more persistent European-session path.

Approaching the European cash open, Tail stays in WATCH because liquidity and index rebalancing can widen intraday moves. The score assumes no evidence yet of failed retracements or sustained session-extreme holding.

The European opening hour lifts conditional Tail modestly. A directional break would need to hold through meaningful retracements and receive cross-asset confirmation before the risk state moves beyond WATCH.

After the initial European impulse, Tail remains in WATCH if price rotates back into the overnight range. Continued extension with semiconductor and megacap alignment would be the main condition for escalation.
Mid-European trade keeps Tail in WATCH while markets assess whether the opening move has durability. Conflicting breadth or recovery away from an extreme would favor a mixed regime.

Late-morning Europe remains a conditional transition window ahead of the next U.S. data cycle later on September 1. Tail stays near the lower WATCH band unless a persistent overnight-to-Europe trend has already formed.
drivers: Next U.S. data cycle remains outside this forecast horizon
